text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — I noticed ~0.6% of incoming requests are failing validation after we started enforcing the new /v3 payload schema in the canary region. Not sure if these are old SDKs or malformed clients. Can we discuss a safe enforcement plan and what telemetry we should emit?

Lee Park: Which field is causing the failures?

Maria Chen: The server now requires `request.context.env` to be an object instead of a string. Most failures are `schema_error: context.env type` in the logs.

Jamal Rivera: Ah yeah, older clients sent `context.env: "prod"`. We added the object for richer metadata. We should avoid hard 4xx until tenants have a chance to roll.

Ash Patel: +1. Proposal: soft-enforce for 2 weeks — accept old shape but emit `compat.v3.missing_context_object` metric and return a `Warning` header with migration guidance. After 2 weeks flip to strict with 400 + helpful message.

Maria Chen: That seems reasonable. Two concerns: 1) noisy metrics (we'll get a lot of signals), 2) tenant-level enforcement — some customers on Dedicated/Private might want longer windows.

Lee Park: For noisy metrics we can sample — emit full metric for 1% of failures and an aggregated counter for the rest. Also include tenant_id tag so we can target high-impact customers.

Jamal Rivera: Tenant-level override makes sense. We have per-tenant feature flags already. We can add a `compat_v3_strict` flag that defaults to false and can be toggled from Console. Then infra can run a gradual enable per-tenant.

Ash Patel: Telemetry sketch: 
- `compat.v3.missing_context_object.count` (by tenant, sampled)
- `compat.v3.migration_warning_shown.count` (how often we include the Warning header)
- `compat.v3.enforced_errors.count` after flip date
And attach a sample payload (redacted) for debugging when sampling hits.

Maria Chen: For the Warning header content, we should include an explanation + link to migration doc, and a machine-readable header for SDKs to detect e.g. `X-Redwood-Compat: v3-context-object-deprecated`. Something like: `Warning: context.env must be an object; see https://redwood.ai/docs/migrations/v3#context`

Jamal Rivera: Avoid leaking PII in sampled payloads. Use our existing scrubber library before attaching payloads.

Lee Park: What about deploy strategy? We need the gateway to accept both shapes, runtime to emit metrics, and the console to surface top offenders.

Ash Patel: Plan: 
1) Gateway change: schema acceptance logic (accept both shapes) + add `compat-info` header forwarded to backend.
2) Runtime: when backend sees string type, convert to object `{ name: value }` for processing and emit the sampled metric. Also optionally append `X-Redwood-Compat` header so SDKs can detect it during streaming responses.
3) Console: add a discover page listing tenants hitting the compat metric.
4) After 14 days (configurable), flip a gate that makes the gateway reject the string shape with 400.

Maria Chen: Sounds good. Any pushback on converting string->object on the server side? That might hide client bugs and delay proper SDK updates.

Jamal Rivera: True. Convert-on-receive should be opt-in per-tenant. Default conversion enabled for hosted customers to reduce incidents, disabled for Dedicated/Private unless they opt in.

Lee Park: Also add an escape hatch: `Prefer-Compat: legacy-accept` header that tenants can set temporarily if they need more time. That also helps partner teams coordinate.

Ash Patel: Edge case: batched requests — if a batch mixes shapes we need consistent conversion semantics. We'll normalize each item individually and emit per-item metric.

Maria Chen: Good call. Who's owning telemetry + console work vs gateway/runtime?

Lee Park: Infra owns gateway change and header passthrough. Runtime team (Ash) will own conversion and metrics. Console (Jamal) will own surfacing tenants and flag control. I'll coordinate the rollout plan and runbooks.

Jamal Rivera: I'll draft a short migration doc for support with examples: old vs new payload, example Warning header, suggested SDK patch.

deploy-bot: Deploy job queued: infra/gateway/accept-both-shapes -> canary us-west-2. CI: green. :rocket:

Maria Chen: OK let's do canary deploy tomorrow morning, collect 48h of metrics, then provide a blue/green ramp plan. Add an item to the runbook: how to quickly revert to legacy acceptance (feature-flag off) and how to opt specific tenant into extended window.

Ash Patel: I'll prepare a short snippet for SDKs: 
```
if (typeof request.context.env === 'string') {
  // temporary shim for older clients
  request.context.env = { name: request.context.env };
}
```

Lee Park: SGTM. Also add automated alert: if any tenant's sampled failure rate > 0.5% of their total requests for 24h, page oncall and create a support ticket.

Maria Chen: Great. Next steps: 
- Jamal: migration doc + Console tenant list (ETA 48h)
- Ash: runtime conversion + metrics (ETA 48h)
- Lee/Infra: gateway accept-both-shapes canary (ETA 24h)
- Maria: runbook + alert config (ETA 24h)

Jamal Rivera: I'll post the draft doc in #eng-docs when ready.

Maria Chen: Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Lee Park: Thanks — we'll review results after the canary window finishes. :eyes:
